claims.text: The tweet is one sentence from a verified account with about 8,457 followers; when fetched it had 6 likes and 707 views, and it links to no evidence.
Published Tinker rates put $100 at roughly 133M training tokens at 64K context, enough for daily increments but not for repeated full retrains of a large augmented corpus.

Tinker's published rates for Inkling 2 Mini are $0.75 per million training tokens at 64K context and $1.50 at 256K, with sampling at $0.15 per million input tokens, $0.015 cached and $0.50 output; storage is $0.10 per GB-month, and forward-only requests from a training client bill at the training rate.
A free 64K tier lists $0.00 for everything, subject to unspecified rate limits and a positive balance, with no stated end date.
It is a mixture-of-experts model with 26.4B total parameters and 3.4B active per token, rising to 5.4B weight activations once looping is counted.
Its 24 stored layers sit in four blocks of six; the two middle blocks run three times, so 24 stored layers give 48 layer applications per token.
Experts were pruned from 384 to 128, then the model was healed on 1T tokens distilled from a larger internal Inkling model.
The lab reports the non-looped version cost 7.5% less to train but needed 140% more inference compute to match loss.
Most weights are NVFP4 with the last four layers in MXFP8, giving a footprint of about 20GB and a Mac path via Ollama with 32GB or more.
The official announcement as retrieved gives no context window or license, while The Next Web, VentureBeat, The Decoder and Artificial Analysis give 1M tokens and Apache 2.0.
Tinker's own model table lists Inkling 2 Mini at 256K maximum context.
Per-task time is 9 minutes in one report and 14.7 minutes on Artificial Analysis's model page, and output speed is 280 tokens/s in one review and 172 on the Artificial Analysis page.
AA-Omniscience is -8.6 for Inkling against -6.4 for Qwen3.8-27B.
DeepSWE v1.1 42.2 vs 48.2; BrowseComp 61.6 vs 79.0; AutomationBench-AA 48.2 vs 41.8; Non-hallucination rate 71.4 vs 63.4 (Qwen3.8-27B vs Inkling-2-Mini)
The comparison comes from a review that counted 25 wins, 10 losses, 2 ties and 1 split across 38 shared rows, drawn from the vendor table.
Gwern targets over $1,000 a month per user, notes dynamic evaluation costs more than 3x normal usage, a three-model ensemble more than 6x a frozen model, and warns against optimizing for low cost.
The prototype uses a roughly 1GB corpus enriched with LLM-generated annotations, summaries and a `PRINCIPAL.md` profile, because plain finetuning generalizes poorly.
The essay was first published in December 2025 and revised into mid-2026.
The essay does say a sub-100B off-the-shelf model on commodity hardware could do the job, which is the one place Inkling 2 Mini fits his specification.

LTM-Lab's V19 adds an external, disk-backed event store with a small learned working state, not weight updates, and reports in a small pilot: 4/4 on color identification with the source image shown, 1/4 on choosing the right original from four, 0/8 on writing a valid lesson from eight events, 0/82 work-order executions after autonomous intake and 3/82 with verbatim stored sources.
Krause et al. (2017) used gradient descent on recent history to set new word-level perplexity records of 51.1 on Penn Treebank and 44.3 on WikiText-2.
learning-rate re-warming, re-decaying and replay matched full retraining at 405M and 10B scale on weakly shifted data.

An independent study found LoRA "learns less and forgets less": it underperforms full finetuning on code and math, forgets the base less, and full finetuning learns perturbations of rank 10 to 100 times higher than typical LoRA settings.
past that, training efficiency degrades with the ratio of dataset to capacity, and the authors cite roughly 2 bits per parameter of storage.
Gekhman et al. (EMNLP 2024) found examples introducing unfamiliar facts are learned significantly slower than familiar ones and, once learned, linearly increase the model's tendency to hallucinate.

Ovadia et al. compared unsupervised fine-tuning with retrieval and found retrieval consistently outperforms fine-tuning, both for facts seen in pretraining and for wholly new ones; training on many rephrasings of a fact may help.
one proposal builds a single-user evaluation set from continuous screen recordings at 4fps, about 1GB per hour of capture, estimating a year at under 10TB and under $150 of Cloudflare storage.

Forethought's design sketch lists the cost of getting this wrong: unreliable angels are merely annoying, "fallen angel" variants could manipulate users, over-outsourcing risks gradual disempowerment, and deep personal data access raises privacy risk.
The Decoder flags that the "leads open models under 100B" claim is limited to that class and that the Intelligence Index result is a tie with Qwen3.8-27B.
I treat the 1M figure as the weights' native window and 256K as Tinker's training and serving limit; I have not verified that reading directly.
